quotes.text: After the facilitator settles the payment on-chain, Stripe records it as a [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents.md).
Use the deposit address from the previous step as the static `payTo` recipient.
This feature requires the `2026-05-27.preview` API version.
Because you created the deposit address in live mode, this request moves real funds.
You can test your integration without moving real money by using a Stripe [sandbox](https://docs.stripe.com/sandboxes.md) and Base Sepolia, the testnet for Base.

old_evidence.text: Set up the Stripe client with your secret key and set the API version to `2026-03-04.preview`.
Either extract the address from an existing payment header for retries or verification, or create a new PaymentIntent to generate a new deposit address.
// In-memory cache for deposit addresses (TTL: 5 minutes)

findings: The four pinned hashes and numbered file ranges match. The May pinned artifact is a structured quickstart with Node.js/TypeScript code, despite the header naming Node.js/Python. The November capture is a different full document for the same URL and changes the documented workflow. The coding-agent prompt, links and formatting do not establish a product or runtime change (old 1–8 and 73–225, new 42–52). Diff line 352 joins a removed fence and added code comment. Use old 225 and new 158 for meaning.

The root index routes to Stripe (wiki/index.md line 7), then to the machine payments source and concept (wiki/stripe-index.md lines 595–599 and 703). The mapped quickstart links its May original and concept at lines 52–59, and the concept links both quickstart and sibling guide at lines 62–69. The sibling’s same-URL May capture (fully read for the concrete mode/test differences) adds historical corroboration and is not a second mapped source.

The November standalone create-deposit-address endpoint reference (raw/stripe-api-crypto-deposit-address-create-2026-11-07.md:5-15,38-60) describes a Crypto Deposit Address reusable across PaymentIntents and gives a separate 2026-10-28.endive Tempo request example. Its existence and example header are separate from the x402 guide’s live and sandbox preview headers. Retain the guide’s own headers as documented and avoid adopting one as a universal date for other operations.

Source lines 13 and 17–50 accurately identify the May Hono/middleware quickstart but need explicit historical scope. Add a November lifecycle section or locator covering the HTTP 402 challenge, authorized retry, on-chain verification and settlement by the facilitator, then Stripe recording with the transaction hash and returning content after success. The PaymentIntent is a separate recording step, not the original x402 challenge or chain transfer (old 30–51 and 139–183; new 9–11, 24–39 and 141–189).

Distinguish the mainnet sample’s Base eip155:8453 and authenticated CDP facilitator from sandbox Base Sepolia eip155:84532 with a public x402 facilitator. Preserve dated Stripe approval, the stablecoin configuration, and the live purl real-funds warning. The preview version is endpoint and example scoped: 2026-05-27.preview for live address creation and the stated transaction-verification PaymentIntent client, 2026-07-29.preview in the sandbox address example. No demonstrated alternate sandbox PaymentIntent API version (new 13–22, 54–74, 103–123, 141–189 and 192–281).

The November code uses success plus transaction hash in onAfterSettle, converts atomic USDC units to USD cents, skips amounts below a cent in the sample, uses allowed_payment_method_types with crypto and sends the transaction hash as an idempotency key. The code logs the PaymentIntent ID and does not explicitly branch on a returned Stripe status. The lifecycle diagram shows the intended successful sequence. Document what the example records without inferring end-to-end retry guarantees, automatic Stripe capture from the old guide, exact-once behavior or fund availability (new 24–39 and 141–189).

Keep the November USDC list scoped to crypto PaymentIntent transaction_verification across Tempo, Base and Solana. The worked x402 endpoint is USDC on Base and the broader Machine Payments protocol table routes Tempo and Solana to MPP (raw/stripe-payments-machine-2026-11-07.md:41-49). The May sibling USDC table belongs to deposit mode and already lists the same token networks and addresses (raw/stripe-machine-payments-x402-2026.md:223-231). Keep the November card route as MPP.
substantive_changes: Address and lifecycle. May uses the crypto deposit-mode PaymentIntent and dynamic payTo with retry address/cache validation. November precreates a Stripe Base address as static payTo and creates a crypto PaymentIntent in transaction_verification mode only after network settlement (old 30–51, 112–183 and 186–210; new 24–39, 60–87 and 141–189).

Environment, versions and tests. November provides an authenticated CDP Base mainnet implementation branch and an explicit test mode branch using a sandbox deposit address, Base Sepolia test-USDC and a public facilitator. It separates the live purl exercise that moves real money from the no-real-money sandbox and shows different address creation preview headers. The May sibling already referenced CDP as a possible mainnet facilitator (old 18–26 and 53–71, new 54–74 and 192–281, historical sibling 217–221).

Eligibility and feature boundaries. November spells out the Stablecoins and Crypto request and approval, NY exception and outside-US access-request route, and tells readers to integrate MPP for cards alongside stablecoin payments. The USDC contract table now labels transaction_verification rather than the older sibling deposit mode, with matching addresses for the three networks (old 18–26; new 9–22 and 216–224; historical sibling 223–231).
historical_claims_to_preserve: 2026-05-12 old structured UI quickstart, 2026-03-04.preview, crypto payins prerequisite, dynamic deposit-mode PaymentIntent with deposit_options and Base address as next_action.crypto_display_details data, five-minute example cache with distributed production-cache recommendation, test via Base Sepolia and purl. Preserve the old provenance and dated third-party/self-run production facilitator option (old 1–4, 18–51 and 53–225).

Distinct 2026-05-12 same-URL full guide describes automatic deposit-mode capture when payment settles, own US-only acceptance wording, simulator for deposit-mode sandbox and CDP mainnet link. Those are historical guidance for that snapshot (historical sibling 1–23 and 188–231).
conflicts: Source lines 19, 22, 28–50 and wiki/concepts/stripe-machine-payments.md:29,43,67–68 need a reciprocal dated distinction. The May quickstart dynamically derives a fresh Base deposit address from an upfront crypto deposit-mode PaymentIntent, with NodeCache/matched retry address and 2026-03-04.preview. The November worked flow precreates a separate Stripe deposit-address resource outside the core request path, uses it as a static payTo, and writes a transaction_verification PaymentIntent after facilitator settlement. The later document does not show per-payment address uniqueness for this path. Date the older uniqueness/privacy claim at raw/stripe-machine-payments-2026.md:22-28 and preserve it with the older path (old 18–51, 103–183 and 186–210; new 54–74 and 141–189).

Preserve the distinct historical wiki/sources/source-stripe-machine-payments-x402.md:25–31 and raw/stripe-machine-payments-x402-2026.md:188-225 treatment of CDP mainnet compatibility and deposit-mode sandbox testing. The May same-URL webpage describes automatic capture on observing on-chain settlement and uses simulate_crypto_deposit for a sandbox deposit-mode PaymentIntent that does not monitor testnets (raw/stripe-machine-payments-x402-2026.md:4-8,67-73,188-225). The November sandbox route sends Base Sepolia test USDC through the public facilitator and records via the transaction-verification flow. The November live mainnet purl exercise moves real funds (new 192–214 and 226–281). Add bidirectional route warnings between history and November guidance so the old sandbox limitation does not override the new facilitator test and vice versa.

Record eligibility as dated at wiki/concepts/stripe-machine-payments.md:45 and the source route. The May machine overview excludes New York and Texas and the May historical guide has US-only acceptance wording (raw/stripe-machine-payments-2026.md:22-28, raw/stripe-machine-payments-x402-2026.md:12-23). The November x402 and Machine Payments overview describe all US states except New York and an outside-US request for 30+ countries, with account approval (new 13–22, raw/stripe-payments-machine-2026-11-07.md:41-56). The text does not establish enrollment or eligibility for a specific business.
unresolved_questions: The November guide shows 2026-05-27.preview for live address and transaction-verification calls and 2026-07-29.preview for sandbox address creation. It provides no alternate sandbox PaymentIntent SDK header or compatibility matrix across those examples. The separate endpoint reference’s 2026-10-28.endive example does not resolve this guide-specific boundary.

The pinned snapshots do not verify payment execution, merchant enrollment, current facilitator SDK or API availability, Stripe status handling beyond the shown code, failure recovery/delivery semantics, or payout timing.

source_assessments.reason: The mapped summary is a useful May overview but its undifferentiated dynamic-address flow, facilitator options and testnet details would send a November implementer to the wrong PaymentIntent mode. Preserve May provenance and add the November lifecycle, scope and reciprocal warnings.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/x402, new raw lines 9-39 describe a server challenging with HTTP 402 and a Stripe deposit address, a client retry with payment authorization, facilitator verification and on-chain settlement, then a server-side Stripe PaymentIntent record before successful resource delivery. The November guide requires an eligible Stripe account and approved Stablecoins and Crypto access. It documents all US states except New York and an application route for businesses in 30+ countries outside the US. For the Base mainnet example use the authenticated CDP facilitator and a prior Stripe deposit-address resource as a static payTo. After settlement the server uses a transaction hash, Base network and crypto transaction_verification PaymentIntent with a hash idempotency key (new raw lines 13-22, new raw lines 54-87, new raw lines 103-123, new raw lines 141-189). The May quickstart instead uses 2026-03-04.preview to create a deposit-mode PaymentIntent for an address before payment, reuses validated cached retry addresses and illustrates Base Sepolia (old raw lines 18-51, old raw lines 103-183, old raw lines 186-210). source-stripe-machine-payments-x402-quickstart.md lines 13–50 largely reflects that May implementation and omits the later address, recording, access and environment boundaries.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/x402, substantive changes are the precreated static Base recipient, post-settlement transaction_verification record, CDP Base mainnet walkthrough, access wording and separate sandbox versus live test paths. The coding-agent prompt, links and formatting are guidance and presentation. Preserve the May 2026-03-04.preview dynamic deposit-mode quickstart and the May sibling's deposit-mode simulator and auto-capture guidance as dated, and add reciprocal warnings in source-stripe-machine-payments-x402-quickstart.md and the Stripe Machine Payments concept. In November, 2026-05-27.preview appears for live address creation and is stated for recording, while sandbox address creation shows 2026-07-29.preview. Live purl moves real funds. Sandbox uses Base Sepolia test USDC and a public facilitator without CDP signup. The token table lists Tempo, Base and Solana for the PaymentIntent recording mode, while the example x402 protocol uses USDC on Base and routes cards to MPP. The old New York and Texas/US-only availability claims should stay with their May authorities, and the later request route does not prove account approval. A chain settlement and recording response do not establish balance availability, payout or exact-once delivery (old raw lines 18-51, old raw lines 53-71, old raw lines 112-183, new raw lines 9-22, new raw lines 24-39, new raw lines 54-74, new raw lines 141-189, new raw lines 192-281).
